reference_class: State with the single coldest 24-hour minimum temperature among US weather stations on July 31, per Ogimet ranking, years 2019-2025
reasoning: Historical July 31 base rate (2019-2025, n=5 via Ogimet): Alaska 2/5, New Hampshire 2/5, Minnesota 1/5, Colorado/Nevada 0/5 (though Colorado won nearby dates in other months). Very recent 2026 daily rankings show Alaska (Jun 20, Jul 8) and Colorado (Jul 1, Jul 5) alternating as coldest, an unusually strong recent Colorado run. CPC Week 3-4 outlook calls for a western ridge (above-normal temps, Alaska and CO/UT border) and a developing monsoon over the Four Corners by mid-late July, which should add cloud/moisture to Colorado and suppress its radiational-cooling edge by month's end, while implying a compensating cooler pattern further east that favors NH/MN historically. No market found on Polymarket/Kalshi for this exact state-ranking contract; only unrelated city-level daily temp markets exist, so no market blend applied.
what_would_change_my_mind: CPC 8-14 day update showing the monsoon/ridge pattern breaking down before July 31, keeping Colorado's high valleys dry and clear
A forecast cold-air intrusion into interior Alaska or the Northeast in the final week of July
Ogimet rankings for July 20-30, 2026 showing a consistent single-state leader emerging

sources: Polymarket/Kalshi search — no matching state-level market found

question: What state will have the hottest temperature on July 31, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves as the state with the weather station recording the highest maximum temperature in the United States according to [Ogimet](https://www.ogimet.com/ranking.phtml.en) on July 31, 2026. A state other than the three listed resolves as Other.
reference_class: State recording the single hottest SYNOP-network station in the continental US on late-July calendar dates, 2022-2025
reasoning: Reference class: Ogimet's daily hottest-US-station winner on late-July dates in recent years, dominated by AZ (Phoenix Sky Harbor, which won the exact analog date July 31 2025 at 109.9F) with NV (Las Vegas/Laughlin, record 120F in 2024) as the main rival and TX a secondary contender. Death Valley/CA rarely appears since Ogimet uses SYNOP airport/military stations, not COOP climate stations (consistent with the May 31 2026 example sweeping all-Texas, no CA station). Adjusted down from a pure AZ-dominant base rate because 2026 is transitioning to El Nino (~80% NOAA odds), which tends to weaken the Southwest monsoon ridge over AZ and shift the seasonal 'hot spot' north/toward TX per current long-range outlooks, modestly boosting TX and NV relative to a typical year.
what_would_change_my_mind: A GFS/ECMWF 10-14 day run (available ~July 17-21) showing a heat dome centered directly over the Desert Southwest/Phoenix vs. shifted toward the Great Basin/Mojave or Texas
Confirmation of active monsoon thunderstorm/cloud cover over Phoenix specifically on July 31
A specific Las Vegas or Texas station forecast to exceed 115F on July 31

question: How many jobs will the U.S. economy add in July 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves as the increase in number of employees on nonfarm payrolls, seasonally adjusted, reported by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics at its[ Employment Situation Summary](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm) for July 2026.
reference_class: trailing 12-month average monthly change in U.S. seasonally-adjusted nonfarm payrolls, as of the June 2026 BLS report
reasoning: June 2026 NFP was +57k, which BLS characterized as roughly in line with the trailing-12-month average of +36k — a clear anchor for trend growth. But June included an anomalous -61k leisure/hospitality drop that likely partially mean-reverts, and ISM services employment just moved back into expansion (51.2 from 47.9), a mildly positive signal. Offsetting factors: fading state/local government hiring boost (per Capital Economics, though their forecasts have been running too high all year), immigration-curb effects on labor supply/demand, and tariff-related hiring caution. Initial claims stay low (labor hoarding, 'slow-hire, slow-fire') but continuing claims are drifting up. No mature market gives a firm July-specific consensus this early (survey week hasn't occurred); Polymarket's July contract is still pricing bins near-equal. Landed slightly above the 12-month trend base rate to reflect partial reversion from June's outlier weakness, with wide uncertainty band given this cycle's pattern of large forecast misses (both directions).

question: Will a Tucker Carlson-founded political party file FEC Form 1 before September 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves as **Yes** if, after July 3, 2026 and before September 1, 2026, a Form 1 "Statement of Organization" is filed with the US [Federal Election Commission](https://www.fec.gov/data/filings/?data_type=processed) for any political party founded or co-founded by Tucker Carlson.
reference_class: Prominent political/media figures who publicly announce intent to found a new political party, converting to an actual FEC Form 1 filing naming them as founder within ~2 months
reasoning:
[pooled 4 independent runs [0.14, 0.12, 0.12, 0.08] -> 0.113; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.14)]
Carlson (July 1-2, 2026) only voiced intent to 'help build' a third party, explicitly disclaiming a candidate role and giving no name, treasurer, structure, or timeline. As of July 11 (research date), 10 days later, no further concrete organizational steps have surfaced. Base rate: prominent-figure 'I'm starting a party' announcements that convert to an actual FEC Form 1 naming them as founder within ~8 weeks are uncommon unless the figure already has campaign-finance infrastructure ready to go (Yang/Forward Party filed same-day, but Yang had pre-built PAC/staff). Musk's 2025 'America Party' shows the filing itself is a trivial administrative step that CAN happen within days, but even there verified/legitimate registration was disputed and messy despite Musk publicly claiming he'd 'formed' the party. Carlson's non-candidate stance suggests he's positioning as a promoter/enabler rather than the hands-on organizer who files paperwork quickly. A separate 'We The People Party' exists but doesn't name Carlson as founder; MTG's parallel party talk is a distinct, not-yet-merged effort. Ballot-access deadlines for 2026 midterms have mostly passed, reducing urgency to file immediately (more likely aimed at 2028). Weighing the low technical bar and high media salience against the total absence of concrete steps and Carlson's own vagueness, I lean well below 50% but not negligible given 7 weeks remain and pressure could accelerate.
what_would_change_my_mind: A specific party name, treasurer, or committee announced by Carlson or his team
Reports of lawyers/staff being hired specifically for FEC registration
MTG or another organizationally-experienced figure formally merging efforts with Carlson under one named entity
Any FEC Form 1 filing appearing in FEC's processed filings database naming a party with Carlson credibly reported as founder

missing_evidence: No news after July 3, 2026 shows organizational progress (treasurer, lawyer, filing prep); could not confirm whether 'We The People Party' is formally tied to Carlson
No news after July 3, 2026 indicating any organizational progress (treasurer, lawyer, party name); no confirmation of merger with MTG or 'We The People Party' efforts
No news after July 3, 2026 on concrete organizing steps (treasurer, committee name, legal counsel) was found despite searching.

question: Will the first physical shipment of NVIDIA H200 chips to China be publicly confirmed before July 25, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if, before July 25, 2026, a report from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) states that a shipment of one or more NVIDIA H200 GPUs has physically arrived at, been received by, cleared Chinese customs for, or been delivered to a customer or facility located in mainland China. reference_class: Sequential government approval + logistics chains for a specific, closely-watched export item where 4-5 prior 'imminent shipment' signals over 5 months all failed to convert within their respective short windows
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs [0.08, 0.05, 0.06] -> 0.062; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.08)]
Status quo since Dec 2025 is zero physical H200 deliveries into mainland China despite five-plus months of 'imminent' signals (Feb ship target, March GTC POs, March Beijing 'nod', May US export approvals for 10 firms). Each has failed to convert to actual customs clearance/delivery. As of July 8-11, 2026 (2-5 days before this forecast), Beijing had still not finalized its import quota (reportedly <200k chips) or given final approval, and Reuters reported Chinese customs actively blocking/pausing supplier shipments. Reference class of repeated bureaucratic near-misses each converting to further delay suggests continued NO is far more likely than a full approval->customs->delivery->public-confirmation chain completing in the ~12 days remaining before July 25. Some upside: chips are reportedly pre-staged/manufactured and Beijing sentiment has shifted toward 'poised to approve', so if the quota clears in the next few days, fast delivery to a few pre-cleared firms (Alibaba/ByteDance/DeepSeek) is not impossible.
what_would_change_my_mind: A Reuters/Bloomberg/Nikkei report citing customs data or a named commercial customer confirming physical receipt
Beijing formally publishing finalized H200 import quotas with immediate effect
A specific company (e.g., Alibaba, ByteDance) confirming receipt in earnings or official statement

question: How many cumulative confirmed Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) cases will the DRC have reported per WHO Disease Outbreak News by July 23, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the cumulative number of confirmed Ebola disease (Bundibugyo virus) cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) as stated in the most recent World Health Organization Disease Outbreak News (DON) item published on or before July 23, 2026, in the outbreak series titled "Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus, Democratic Republic of the Congo & Uganda." DON items are listed at https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news . The relevant figure is the count of laboratory-confirmed cases in the DRC only (excluding Uganda, France, or any other country, and excluding probable/suspected cases). For example, if the latest qualifying DON reports "2,350 confirmed cases" in the DRC, this resolves as 2350.
reference_class: This outbreak's own trailing 1-3 week DRC confirmed-case growth rate (cases/day), extrapolated forward through the WHO DON publication lag
reasoning: Latest qualifying WHO DON (DON612, published 3 Jul, as of 1 Jul) reports 1,460 confirmed DRC cases. DON cadence has been ~14 days (19 Jun, 3 Jul), so the next qualifying DON should publish ~17 Jul with data as of ~14-16 Jul. Trailing growth rate has been ~40-47 cases/day (19 Jun-8 Jul), with a softer 27/day in the most recent 8-11 Jul window that is likely reporting lag rather than true deceleration, given outbreak has just spread to a 5th province and is described as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record. Extrapolating the trend forward to the expected next-DON reporting date gives ~2000-2150; skewed slightly upward for risk of DON publication slipping later (accumulating more days) or further acceleration, balanced against response-driven deceleration or a data revision like the one seen in early June.
what_would_change_my_mind: Publication of DON613 with an actual figure
A sudden deceleration reported in an ECDC CDTR (week 29/30) suggesting response is bending the curve
A downward data revision/cleanup like the one WHO/CDC made in early June
WHO shifting to weekly DON cadence given PHEIC status, which would move the qualifying data-as-of date later and raise the count

question: How many named storms will the 2026 Eastern Pacific hurricane season have had through July 23, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves as the cumulative number of named storms (systems assigned a name from the Eastern Pacific 2026 name list: Amanda, Boris, Cristina, Douglas, Elida, Fausto, Genevieve, Hernan, Iselle, Julio, Karina, Lowell, Marie, Norbert, and onward) in the 2026 Eastern Pacific hurricane season (basin east of 140°W) that had been named on or before July 23, 2026 (UTC), according to the U.S. National Hurricane Center. Resolution uses the season summary table at https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/index.php?season=2026&basin=epac — count each listed storm whose start date is July 23, 2026 or earlier. A system counts if the NHC designated it as a named tropical (or subtropical) storm at any point on or before July 23, 2026, even if it later dissipated. As of July 10, 2026, four named storms had formed (Amanda, Boris, Cristina, Douglas), so a final count of six would resolve as "6". If the NHC summary table has not been updated to reflect a storm that formed by July 23, resolution uses the tally reported by NHC advisories or other [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
reference_class: NHC 1991-2020 climatological normal formation dates for the Nth Eastern Pacific named storm (5th ~Jul 22-23, 6th ~late July), adjusted for this season's observed ~1-2 week head start
reasoning: As of 2026-07-13 (NHC data, fetched directly), 4 named storms have formed (Amanda, Boris, Cristina, Douglas), running ~1-2 weeks ahead of climatological pace. NHC's Jul 12 Tropical Weather Outlook lists a disturbance south of Mexico at 90% formation chance within 7 days (would be Elida, #5) and a second system off southern/SW Mexico at 60% within 7 days, developing by mid-week (would be Fausto, #6) - both windows close by ~Jul 19, leaving buffer before the Jul 23 cutoff. Climatology (per question background) puts the 5th storm right at Jul 22-23 and 6th near month-end, but this year's earlier pacing plus two concrete high-probability disturbances in the pipeline pull the distribution toward 5-6 storms, with real but smaller odds of a 7th given the basin's active July pattern. No credible market (Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold) was found pricing this specific EPac named-storm-count question, so no market blend was applied.

question: Will Marine Le Pen poll at or above 34% in the first round of the most recent 2027 French presidential voting-intention poll listed on Wikipedia before July 25, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if, in the single most recent qualifying first-round voting-intention poll for the 2027 French presidential election listed in the first-round polling tables of the English Wikipedia article "Opinion polling for the 2027 French presidential election" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_for_the_2027_French_presidential_election) as of 23:59 UTC on July 24, 2026, Marine Le Pen's reported first-round voting-intention figure is 34.0% or higher; it resolves NO if that figure is 33.9% or lower. A "qualifying poll" is one that reports a specific first-round voting-intention percentage for Marine Le Pen by name as the National Rally (Rassemblement National) candidate; polls that instead test Jordan Bardella or a generic/unnamed RN candidate do not qualify. "Most recent" is determined by the end date of the poll's fieldwork. If that single poll reports more than one first-round scenario or a range for Le Pen, the highest Le Pen figure among them is used (for example, a reported Le Pen figure of 34% resolves YES).
reference_class: Qualifying (Le Pen named as RN candidate) first-round 2027 French presidential polls listed on the Wikipedia tracking page, July 2026 post-candidacy-announcement subset
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs [0.91, 0.91, 0.91] -> 0.910; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.91)]
Base rate over the 5 qualifying Le Pen-named first-round polls fielded 7-10 July 2026 (immediately post-candidacy-announcement): 35%, 37%, 35%, 35%, 36% — all comfortably above 34%, mean ~35.6%. Broader 2026 reference class including the pre-announcement April/May reading (Ipsos 32%, Harris 32-33%) pulls the unconditional base rate down to ~35.0%, but the conditioning variable (candidacy now confirmed, ~11 days of momentum since 7 July) argues for weighting the tighter post-announcement cluster, whose floor is 35%, not the wider range. For the Elabe poll (current most-recent by fieldwork end date, listed above Verian in the table) to resolve NO, either a new poll must supersede it by 24 July with a sub-34% Le Pen figure, or the resolving poll must be misread. Given 5/5 recent named-Le Pen polls print >=35% with no sign yet of the honeymoon fading within days, and French pollsters typically release every 1-2 weeks (implying 1-3 more polls could appear before 24 July), the main risk is a lower-house-effect pollster (e.g., one similar to the April Harris reading) printing sub-34% before the deadline. That risk is real but a minority scenario given the current unanimous cluster.
what_would_change_my_mind: A new poll fielded after 10 July 2026 (before 24 July) from a historically lower-Le Pen-leaning house (e.g., a repeat of the April Harris Interactive-style 32-33% reading) becoming the most recent by fieldwork end date
Evidence the post-announcement bump is already fading in subsequent daily/weekly tracking
A pollster switching back to testing only Bardella (not Le Pen) as the sole RN scenario, changing which poll qualifies

question: Will a US–Iran ceasefire be in effect on July 23, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if, on July 23, 2026, there is a publicly announced ceasefire, truce, or cessation of hostilities between the United States and Iran that both governments have accepted or publicly stated they are observing, AND no direct military strike by US forces against targets in Iran, or by Iranian forces against US military personnel or installations, has occurred during the three calendar days of July 21, 22, and 23, 2026 (UTC). It resolves NO otherwise — including if no ceasefire is in place, if hostilities are ongoing, or if either side conducts a direct military strike against the other during July 21–23, 2026 (UTC). Resolution will be based on reporting from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) and official US and Iranian government statements. Attacks conducted solely by third parties or non-state proxies not acting as agents of the US or Iranian governments do not by themselves count as strikes between the two states.
reference_class: This conflict's own ceasefire-collapse-recovery cycles (April truce, June MOU) and general wartime ceasefires publicly declared 'over' by a head of state during active tit-for-tat strikes
reasoning: Status quo as of July 13, 2026 is active, escalating hostilities: US struck ~140 Iranian targets July 11-12 and again in early hours of July 13; Iran retaliated against US-linked sites in Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman. Trump publicly declared the ceasefire 'over' on July 8/10 — per the question's fine print, this declaration standing as of July 23 forces NO regardless of later strikes, unless walked back and superseded by a fresh mutually-observed ceasefire. This is the conflict's 4th ceasefire-collapse cycle (April truce collapsed, June 17 MOU collapsed July 7-8); prior recoveries took 6-10 weeks, not the ~8-10 days available before the July 21-23 window. Core dispute (Strait of Hormuz control) is unresolved and driving daily strikes. Diplomatic tracks (Oman talks, Pakistan/Qatar mediation) remain open and Trump has said he doesn't want long-term war, giving nonzero but modest odds of a fast reversal. Even if a new ceasefire were announced, holding with zero strikes for the specific July 21-22-23 window is a further hurdle, though the fine print's allowance for isolated/accidental incidents softens this.
what_would_change_my_mind: A new publicly announced and mutually-accepted ceasefire/truce within the next few days
A Trump or Iranian government statement walking back the 'ceasefire is over' declaration
A sustained lull (3+ days with no strikes) beginning before July 21
Breakthrough at Oman/Switzerland talks specifically resolving the Strait of Hormuz dispute
Signs of exhaustion/de-escalation pressure e.g. from oil price spikes or allied Gulf states

reference_class: UK elections where major parties (Labour/Con/LD) conventionally decline to contest a seat held by a single high-profile figure standing again, leaving only fringe/minor-party opposition ('Speaker seat' precedent: Bercow Buckingham 2010 & 2015 GEs, Hoyle Chorley 2019 GE)

question: How many large active wildfires will NIFC report in its Incident Management Situation Report on July 24, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves as the total number of active large fires reported in the National Interagency Coordination Center's Incident Management Situation Report (IMSR) dated July 24, 2026, published at https://www.nifc.gov/nicc-files/sitreprt.pdf . The intended figure is the nationwide total of active large fires (the sum of uncontained large fires plus contained large incidents still being managed) — the same total that, in the July 10, 2026 report, equaled 38 large fires, which would resolve as 38. This is the count reported in the summary/geographic-area breakdown, NOT the number of new large fires reported that day, the year-to-date number of fires, or acres burned. If the IMSR is not published for the July 24, 2026 reporting date, the value from the most recent IMSR published on or before July 24, 2026 will be used.
reference_class: NIFC IMSR nationwide active large-fire counts in late July during PL4/PL5 (severe, above-average) fire seasons
reasoning: Trend: 38 large fires (Jul 10) -> 44 (Jul 12), a ~16% rise in 2 days, against a backdrop of PL4 (raised from PL3 on Jun 18, PL4 on Jun 29), YTD fires/acres 130-157% above 10-yr average, and an expanding heat dome bringing extreme heat/red-flag conditions to the Intermountain West, N. Great Plains, and Great Basin through mid-late July. The 'large fires' count includes contained-but-still-managed incidents, which tends to make it sticky/upward-biased during active season since new ignitions often outpace full closeout. Countervailing: SW monsoon (above-average precip forecast, though onset timing uncertain) could bring some relief, though it mainly affects AZ/NM rather than the currently hardest-hit UT/CO/OR/WA/AK. I carry ~15-20% that CDC posts same-day on Thu Aug 6 (two increments), and ~3% that an update is skipped (stays 35). Counter-case for a higher number: outbreak identification is lumpy and 2026 is a record year with importation-driven clusters, so a +3/+4 week is live; counter-case for lower: the huge SC outbreak is closed and most new cases attach to existing 2025/2026 outbreaks rather than founding new ones. Evidence is moderately thin on the exact publish-day rule (one corroborated data point plus the question's own conflicting 'typically Wednesdays' boilerplate), so I keep mass on 35-36 rather than extrapolating two increments. No prediction market prices the outbreak count.
what_would_change_my_mind: Direct observation of the CDC page publishing an update on the same Thursday as its 'as of' date (would shift mass to two increments, median ~37-38)
The as-of-July-30 update itself, once posted (a +3 or more would move the whole distribution up ~2)
Evidence that the page reverted to a Wednesday publish with a same-week as-of date, which would make an Aug-5-dated update the last one before resolution
News of several newly identified multi-case clusters (e.g. camp- or travel-associated) in late July, signalling a lumpy high week
Any CDC reporting disruption, schedule change, or annulment-triggering removal of the outbreak counter

question: How many locally acquired human West Nile virus cases will ECDC report in Europe for the 2026 season in its early-August surveillance update?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves as the cumulative number of locally acquired (autochthonous) human West Nile virus infections reported across all EU/EEA and neighbouring countries for the 2026 transmission season, as shown in the ECDC weekly surveillance overview "Surveillance of West Nile virus infections in humans in Europe" (2026 season), reached from the ECDC West Nile virus infection topic page (https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/west-nile-virus-infection). The value is the Europe-wide total number of human cases (probable and confirmed combined) shown in the map/table of the most recent ECDC weekly update dated on or before 7 August 2026. For example, a reported cumulative total of 150 human cases resolves as 150. If ECDC's 2026 weekly page is unreachable, the figure will be taken from the cumulative case total for the same period in the EFSA-ECDC monthly West Nile virus report or as reported by credible sources (https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions); if no such figure is published, the question is annulled.
reference_class: ECDC weekly seasonal surveillance reports, Europe (EU/EEA + neighbouring countries): cumulative locally acquired human West Nile virus cases at the first-week-of-August data cutoff, 2015-2025 seasons
reasoning: ECDC's 24 July 2026 report (data to 22 July) shows 81 locally acquired cases across 6 countries (Italy 46, Greece 21, N. Macedonia 5, Romania 5, Spain 3, France 1), up from 33-34 a week earlier. Reference-class prior: ECDC/EFSA state the past-decade average cumulative at the early-August cutoff is 163 (2025 was 202; 2024 was 69 on 31 July en route to 1,436). 2026 is running ahead of that pace, and Italy's spread is unusually wide for late July (20 regions incl. Milan and Rome), so I scale the 163 anchor up. Two frames converge on ~225-245 for a 5 August data cutoff: weekly multipliers decaying from 2.4 to ~1.9 then ~1.6, and a country-level build (Italy ~130, Greece ~48, rest ~50). The dominant uncertainty is not epidemiology but which report resolves: 7 Aug is a Friday publication day (data to 5 Aug, ~230), but the scheduled 00:00 UTC resolution stamp precedes it, in which case the 31 July report (data to 29 July, ~145) governs. I weight 65/35 toward the 7 Aug report, which lowers the median to ~195 and fattens the left flank. Counterargument to my central case: part of the 33->81 jump may be reporting catch-up rather than true acceleration, which would flatten the next two weeks; the 10th percentile of 118 covers a slow week plus the early-report branch.
what_would_change_my_mind: The ECDC weekly report published 31 July 2026 (data to 29 July) — a value near 110-125 would signal deceleration and pull the median toward ~160; a value above 170 would push it toward ~280
Confirmation of which report the resolver uses (7 Aug Friday publication vs. the 00:00 UTC 7 Aug stamp) — collapsing that 65/35 mixture either way shifts the median by ~40-50 cases
Italian national (ISS bollettino) or Greek EODY weekly counts for weeks 31-32 diverging sharply from the ECDC-reported trajectory
Reports of a new large national cluster (Serbia, Hungary, Romania) or a heatwave/cold-snap signal materially changing vector activity in the Po Valley and Attica

question: How many transit calls will IMF PortWatch report for the Strait of Hormuz on August 2, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the number of daily transit calls (arrivals of ships) recorded for the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint on the calendar date August 2, 2026, as reported by IMF PortWatch. The value can be read from the IMF PortWatch Port Monitor (https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/port-monitor — select the "Chokepoints" view, then "Strait of Hormuz", and read the daily "Transit Calls" value for August 2, 2026), which draws on PortWatch's underlying Daily Chokepoint Transit Calls dataset (ArcGIS item id 42132aa4e2fc4d41bdaf9a445f688931). PortWatch updates chokepoint data weekly on Tuesdays at approximately 9:00 AM US Eastern Time, so the August 2, 2026 value is expected in the update published on Tuesday, August 4, 2026. For example, if PortWatch reports 28 ships transited the Strait of Hormuz on August 2, 2026, this resolves as 28.
reference_class: Daily IMF PortWatch transit calls for the Strait of Hormuz during the 2026 crisis period (March-July 2026), conditioned on being ~1 week after a local trough
reasoning: Reference class: daily PortWatch Hormuz transit calls during the 2026 crisis (Mar-Jul 2026), whose crisis-period daily median is ~10-12 with enormous dispersion (7DMA swung 2.7 -> 51 -> 28 -> 15 within months). Current state is a deep trough: Lloyd's counted 53 transits in the week to Jul 20 (-66% w/w), Kpler 3/day Jul 22-24, Windward 1 vessel Jul 25, under a reinstated US blockade. PortWatch counts more broadly than these commercial trackers (15 on Jul 19 vs ~3-4/day non-Iran-linked), so its current level is likely ~6-10/day, not 3. Against persistence: US strikes paused Jul 25 after 13 nights, Iran-Oman technical talks on a dual-corridor scheme were reported progressing Jul 26, and ~1,500 backlogged ships could release fast - the Jun 17 MOU took traffic from ~5/day to 51 in a week. Counterargument: every prior deal (April ceasefire, Jun 17 MOU) collapsed within weeks, and a deal landing after ~Jul 30 leaves too little lag for Aug 2 to respond. Mixture: ~30% re-escalation (0-8), ~35% quiet-but-no-deal drift (3-18), ~35% deal-driven rebound (8-45). Tails kept wide deliberately; upper tail is capped well below the ~90 pre-crisis norm since even the best post-MOU stretch averaged 28/day.
what_would_change_my_mind: A formal US-Iran or Iran-Oman corridor agreement announced before ~Jul 30 with insurers/operators publicly resuming Gulf calls - would shift the median toward 20-25
Resumption of nightly US strikes or a new tanker sinking in the Jul 28-Aug 1 window - would pull the median to 3-4
The Jul 28 PortWatch release showing Jul 20-26 dailies well above ~10, indicating a higher structural floor than the Kpler/Windward commercial counts suggest
Kalshi/Polymarket 'normal by Aug 31' pricing moving decisively (below ~25% or above ~70%)

question: What state will have the hottest temperature on August 31, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves as the state with the weather station recording the highest maximum temperature in the United States according to [Ogimet](https://www.ogimet.com/ranking.phtml.en) on August 31, 2026. A state other than the three listed resolves as Other.
reference_class: State of the highest-max-temperature US station in the Ogimet SYNOP ranking on August 31, years 2018-2025 (n=7 retrieved: AZ 6, TX 1), conditioned on the current restricted major-airport station pool

No human market exists (Kalshi/Polymarket price city-level daily highs, not this contract), so no crowd anchor. question: Will KEPCO have publicly disclosed a specific identified cause of the Ohi-3 field-loss reactor shutdown by August 20, 2026?

A disclosure meets this standard if it names a concrete fault at the component level or narrower — for example a field breaker, exciter, brushes/collector rings, a short/ground/break in a specific field circuit, or an instrumentation or protection-relay malfunction. A statement that merely repeats that the cause is "under investigation" (調査中), or that describes only the general phenomenon or a broad subsystem (e.g., "an abnormality in the generator excitation/field system" or "excitation equipment") without naming a concrete component or mechanism, does NOT count. question: What will PAHO report as the cumulative confirmed measles case count for the Region of the Americas in 2026, in its most recent situation report available on August 21, 2026?

reference_class: Successive PAHO measles situation reports / epidemiological alerts within the same outbreak year (2026 reports #1-#8 and the Feb/May/Aug alerts): the regional cumulative confirmed figure in the next report published ~2 weeks later = prior report's figure + observed inter-report accrual
reasoning: The question's background is stale by ~25,000 cases. Reference class is successive PAHO measles reports within an outbreak year: the next report equals the last figure plus 2-week accrual, so the anchor is 47,459 status-quo. Current accrual has decelerated (non-Guatemala ~270/wk; Mexico added 4 confirmed in EW31; Guatemala +769 in 12 days nationally), so Sitrep #9 on the clean 14-day cadence (~14 Aug, covering EW31) should read roughly 48,000-49,000; ~30% weight that no new doc qualifies and 47,459 stands. Cross-document revisions are small and can go slightly negative (Guatemala 30,371 -> 30,040), so a fall below 42,000 would require PAHO to revert to a lab-confirmed-only definition - not a mechanism I can see. My true EV is ~48,500; p_above_upper is genuinely ~0.97 but is capped at 0.5, so the in-range percentiles are packed against the upper bound. No prediction market prices this contract: Polymarket's ~100 measles markets are US-only CDC thresholds (wrong geography, source, and resolution), so they are near-miss evidence, not an anchor.

A downward restatement of Guatemala's count if PAHO stops counting clinical-criterion cases as confirmed, which is the only realistic path back toward the stated 23,000-42,000 range
Evidence that situation reports are NOT listed on the Epidemiological Alerts and Updates page and a resolver reads the criterion strictly, locking the answer to the 7 Aug alert's 47,459

question: What will the Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey current general activity diffusion index read for August 2026?

The value can be found on the Philadelphia Fed's survey page: https://www.philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/regional-economic-analysis/manufacturing-business-outlook-survey . For example, a reported value of 41.4 resolves as 41.4, and a value of -5.2 resolves as -5.2.
reference_class: Months immediately following a Philadelphia Fed MBOS current general activity print of 35 or higher, 2000-2025 (Feb 2004, Mar 2011, Apr 2011, Mar 2017, Apr 2021, May 2021, Dec 2021, Feb 2025)
reasoning: July printed 41.4, a ~5-year high and a 31-point jump from 10.3, in a series whose 2026 mean is ~18 and whose pure sampling noise is ~7 index points (~100 respondents) — so a large give-back is the modal outcome. Reference class of the 8 post-≥35 months since 2000 averaged ~30 next month (range 15.4-50.2, SD~12); an AR(1) around a 2026 regime mean of 18 with rho~0.35 gives ~26. Unlike the classic reversion cases, the backdrop is genuinely strong: ISM 55.6 in July (best since May 2022), production 58.5, employment expanding, S&P Global PMI at a 4-year high — that raises the floor. Offsetting: MBOS future activity fell 16 pts to 34.4, consensus/model forecasts cluster near 25, and this series gaps violently downward (Apr 26.7 -> May -0.4), so the left tail is fatter than the right. No human prediction market exists on this contract (checked Kalshi, Polymarket, Manifold); the only external number is a Trading Economics model near 25, which I treat as weak confirmation, not an anchor. Median 26, wide bands (SD~13) with left skew; escape mass priced small: >55 needs a further acceleration past the modern-era high (3%), <-25 needs a COVID-scale 66-point collapse inside the Aug 10-17 collection window with no such shock visible (1%).
what_would_change_my_mind: A sharp macro/market shock or tariff escalation between Aug 10-17 that hits the collection window
Empire State August (released ~Aug 17) printing sharply negative or sharply higher, as a same-window regional read
Evidence that the July jump was concentrated in a handful of large respondents or a seasonal-adjustment artifact

question: How many political prisoners will Foro Penal report in Venezuela as of August 20, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves as the number displayed under "Presos políticos" on the homepage of the Venezuelan NGO Foro Penal (https://foropenal.com/) as of the most recent update on or before August 20, 2026. For example, if the site shows "382 Presos políticos," the question resolves as 382. If Foro Penal states a cutoff date for its figure, use the most recent figure whose cutoff date is on or before August 20, 2026; otherwise use the figure displayed on the homepage on August 20, 2026. If no such figure is reported by Foro Penal on its website or official social media accounts, the question is annulled.
reference_class: Two-week changes in Foro Penal's running Venezuelan political-prisoner tally during the post-amnesty stall regime (June-August 2026), i.e. the weekly balances 404 -> 372 -> 379 -> 382
reasoning: Foro Penal publishes weekly with a Monday cutoff and ~2-3 day lag, so the resolving figure is the 17 Aug cutoff (likely published ~19 Aug) or, if it slips, the 10 Aug one - one to two weekly steps from the current 382. The post-amnesty release wave has stalled since early July: 372 (6 Jul) -> 379 (27 Jul) -> 382 (3 Aug), a net +2.5/week as new detentions and newly-documented older cases outpace trickle releases. Continuing that drift over 1-2 weeks lands ~385-387. The one genuine downside catalyst is the US-facilitated dialogue table (convened 1 Aug, first meeting 6 Aug, first cycle to 12 Aug) where prisoner release is the opposition's headline demand - but that cycle was scoped to methodology, and 2026's record is systematic underdelivery (Feb's order to free 379 yielded 19 confirmed; May's promised 500+ did not materialize), plus Foro Penal only de-lists after verification. So the left tail is fat but not central: 8% below 329.5. Upside escape is thin - the largest weekly add in this regime is +14, so +49 in two weeks needs a regime break: 3%. Main counterargument: a transitional government under US pressure could execute a confidence-building release of 50-150 at any moment, which is exactly why I skew the inside distribution left rather than centering symmetrically on 386. No prediction market prices this quantity.

question: How many SpaceX Falcon 9 launches will occur between August 20 and August 21, 2026 (inclusive)?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves as the number of SpaceX Falcon 9 orbital launch attempts with a liftoff timestamped (UTC) on August 20 or August 21, 2026, as recorded in the main launch log table of the Wikipedia article "List of Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launches" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Falcon_9_and_Falcon_Heavy_launches). Every Falcon 9 flight that reaches the point of engine ignition/liftoff counts, regardless of whether the mission subsequently succeeds or fails; Falcon Heavy flights and Starship flights do not count. For example, if two Falcon 9 flights lift off on August 20 and one on August 21, the question resolves 3.
reference_class: Rolling 2-day UTC windows during SpaceX's sustained 2026 Falcon 9 cadence (49 Falcon-9-only liftoffs observed Apr 11 - Aug 8, 2026, Falcon Heavy excluded)
reasoning: Base rate dominates: 49 Falcon 9 liftoffs in the 120 days Apr 11-Aug 8 2026 (Launch Library 2 record) = 0.408/day, cross-checked by 'the 90th Falcon 9 flight of the year' on Aug 4 (0.417/day) and Wikipedia's 687 cumulative Falcon-family figure as of Aug 8. That gives lambda ~0.82 per 2-day window. Crucially the empirical 2-day-window distribution is under-dispersed vs Poisson (37 zeros / 68 ones / 14 twos / zero threes over 119 windows) because pad turnaround floors and a metronomic manifest keep windows at 0 or 1; I blended ~55/45 toward the empirical shape while retaining a thin 3+ tail. Published schedules list flights through Aug 19 (Starlink 17-50, VSFB 02:00 UTC) and nothing on Aug 20-21, but that is a T-10 listing artifact, not a real gap - unannounced Starlink missions fill in, and Vandenberg's Aug 19 slot can slip into Aug 20 (~20-25%). Pad-level bottom-up agrees: VSFB is on ~4.4-day turnaround so its next flight after Aug 19 is ~Aug 23, while the Cape is due ~Aug 21-22 off its Aug 16 Globalstar flight. No Falcon 9 grounding or anomaly in effect (searched, absent); the Aug 10 Starlink 10-19 scrub was routine weather/technical. No human market prices this 2-day window - Kalshi's monthly SpaceX count market (~98% for >10, ~93% for >11 in August) is a near-miss contract on window, vehicle scope, and resolution source, so I used it only as corroboration that ~0.4-0.45/day is the consensus cadence, not as an anchor. Main counterargument for a lower number: five flights are already packed into Aug 10-19, and if August's total lands near 13 the back third could be sparse - but reading a partly-populated forward manifest as a real trough is the classic error here, so I only nudged the EV down from 0.83 to 0.82.
what_would_change_my_mind: A Falcon 9 anomaly, FAA grounding, or fleet stand-down announced between now and Aug 20 (would push most mass to 0)
Public schedules (Spaceflight Now / nextspaceflight / rocketlaunch.org) adding one or two firm Falcon 9 missions dated Aug 20 or Aug 21 as the manifest firms up inside T-7
The Aug 19 Starlink 17-50 Vandenberg flight scrubbing on the 19th, which would drop it directly into the window
Hurricane or major Eastern Range weather/maintenance closure affecting Cape Canaveral in the Aug 18-22 period
A sustained cadence break in the Aug 10-19 flights (e.g. only 2 of the 5 scheduled actually flying), indicating the underlying rate has fallen below ~0.4/day

Falcon Heavy launches do NOT count; only Falcon 9 launches count. For example, if 97 Falcon 9 launches have lifted off in this window, this resolves as 97.
reference_class: Rolling ~10-day windows of SpaceX Falcon 9 liftoffs during 2026 year-to-date (92 launches over 221 days, 0.416/day), cross-checked against the trailing-30-day rate and against forward-manifest realization rates for SpaceX launch schedules 10 days out

question: Will Central Park record measurable precipitation on August 20, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if the official National Weather Service Central Park, NY station (KNYC) records at least 0.01 inch of precipitation for the calendar day of August 20, 2026 (US Eastern local calendar day), and NO otherwise. Resolution will use the daily precipitation total for Central Park as reported by NOAA's xmACIS2 tool (https://xmacis.rcc-acis.org/) for station "NY City Central Park" for August 20, 2026; a "T" (trace) or 0.00 entry resolves NO. If xmACIS2 is unavailable, the NWS New York (OKX) Daily Climate Report (CLI) for Central Park (https://www.weather.gov/wrh/climate?wfo=okx) or other credible sources reporting the official Central Park daily total will be used.
reference_class: Calendar day August 20 at NWS Central Park (KNYC), 1950-2025, daily precipitation >=0.01in (trace and 0.00 count as no), plus all August days at KNYC under 1991-2020 normals
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs [0.36, 0.32, 0.34] -> 0.340; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.36)]
Base rate first: Central Park recorded >=0.01in on Aug 20 in 21 of 76 years (27.6%, 1950-2025, ACIS), consistent with August normals of ~9.4-10 measurable days per 31 (~30-32%); the date-specific dip is within sampling noise (SE ~5pp). Lead time is 10 days, where deterministic skill is near zero, so climatology dominates. Modest upward adjustments: CPC's Day 8-14 hazards product (issued Aug 9, valid Aug 17-23) flags a slight risk of heavy precipitation for portions of the Northeast/Mid-Atlantic specifically Mon-Thu Aug 17-20; ECMWF ENS has 21/50 and GEFS 14/30 members at >=0.01in grid-box precip for Aug 20 (~42-47% raw), though model light-precip over-frequency inflates this versus a point gauge - at a 0.05in grid threshold the same members give 23-28%, bracketing climatology. August 2026 is running wet at Central Park (3.14in and 5 measurable days through Aug 9). Counter-evidence: the Open-Meteo best-match deterministic blend and GFS operational are dry on Aug 20 (0.00in, 19% PoP), NHC sees no tropical system reaching the East Coast within 7-10 days, and Kalshi's monthly Central Park rainfall book implies only about-normal precipitation for the rest of August. Landing a few points above the ~30% climatological anchor, discounting the raw ensemble fraction heavily for day-10 skill and area-vs-point bias.
what_would_change_my_mind: A 3-7 day NWS OKX/WPC forecast (once Aug 20 enters that range) showing a well-defined front, tropical moisture plume, or closed low timed for Aug 20 over the NYC metro

ECMWF/GEFS ensemble measurable-precip fraction for Aug 20 moving decisively outside the 30-50% band on successive runs, or member QPF distributions shifting so most wet members exceed 0.10in rather than 0.01-0.03in
Development of an Atlantic tropical system with a track toward the Mid-Atlantic/Northeast in the Aug 18-22 window
CPC 6-10/8-14 day outlooks flipping the Northeast to strongly below-normal precipitation with ridging/dry Canadian high signal for Aug 19-21
A liquid Kalshi KXRAINNYC daily contract for Aug 20 opening at a price materially away from ~35c

resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if, as of August 21, 2026 (23:59 UTC), the governments of Iran and Oman have both officially confirmed a finalized bilateral agreement or joint statement that designates a specific new shipping route (i.e., designated navigation lanes) for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, as reported by [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/) or other [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). "Finalized and officially confirmed" means both governments (or their foreign ministries) have publicly stated that the agreement text is concluded and issued — not merely that talks are "near", "in final drafting", "a mutual understanding", or a proposal. It resolves NO if, as of that date, no such finalized joint agreement has been officially confirmed by both governments.

reasoning: Reference class: bilateral texts publicly described by one party as 'in final stages/final drafting' that are formally concluded AND jointly confirmed by both governments within ~2 weeks — historically ~30-40%, lower when a third party actively opposes. The binding constraint is Oman, not Iran: Oman's MFA site as of Aug 10 shows no joint statement, only an Aug 8 note that talks are 'progressing constructively', and Muscat has never endorsed Iran's route/toll terms. question: Will Israel have formally accepted the Board of Peace's 15-point second-phase Gaza plan as of September 10, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if, as of September 10, 2026 (23:59 UTC), the Government of Israel has formally accepted the US-backed "Board of Peace" 15-point second-phase Gaza roadmap (which links a gradual Israeli withdrawal to the decommissioning and storage of Hamas weapons under a Palestinian National Committee for the Administration of Gaza). Formal acceptance means an announcement, reported by Reuters or other [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), that the Israeli cabinet, security cabinet, or Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has officially approved, signed, or accepted the 15-point plan (or its NCAG/withdrawal-linked-to-disarmament framework) as the basis for implementing the second phase. Reported acceptance conditioned on later negotiation of implementation details still counts, provided Israel is described as having accepted the plan itself. It resolves NO if, as of that date, Israel has not so accepted the plan, including if Israel continues to reject it, accepts only a materially different plan, or negotiations remain frozen. If credible reporting is genuinely conflicting about whether formal acceptance occurred, the question resolves NO.
reference_class: Head of government formally accepting a specific named peace/withdrawal framework within ~3 weeks of publicly and repeatedly rejecting it, while facing a national election within 10 weeks
reasoning: Status quo is an explicit, deliberately repeated public rejection (Netanyahu, Aug 9: 'Israel rejects the 15-point document', restated for emphasis). Reference class: governments formally accepting a named framework they publicly and emphatically rejected, within a ~3-week window — rare, ~5-8%. Adjusting down: Oct 27 Israeli elections make endorsement of synchronized withdrawal-for-decommissioning coalition-threatening; the Aug 17 four-hour Kushner meeting produced no agreement on key points and the items that were agreed (US general supervising handover, no redeployment/reconstruction until Hamas fully disarmed) are the opposite sequencing, which resolves NO as a 'materially different plan'; ambiguous reporting also resolves NO. Adjusting up modestly: intense active US shuttle diplomacy, Trump's personal stake, and generous fine print counting a renumbered-but-equivalent framework. Main counterargument: a Cairo-brokered repackaging could be reported as Israeli acceptance of the core framework before Sep 10 — but Israel's stated red line (full disarmament first) is precisely what the plan links, and US leverage looks diminished. Thin, one-sided evidence points one way; I stay near a low base rate.
what_would_change_my_mind: Reuters/AP reporting that the Israeli security cabinet has voted to approve the 15-point roadmap or an NCAG/withdrawal-linked-to-disarmament second-phase framework
A Trump-Netanyahu summit or public Trump ultimatum producing an announced Israeli acceptance
Netanyahu publicly committing to the plan as Hamas has demanded, or Israeli officials describing the Cairo track output as acceptance of the Board of Peace framework rather than a substitute

reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs [0.35, 0.22, 0.35] -> 0.303; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.35)]

question: What share of the vote will Michael Minogue receive in the Massachusetts Republican gubernatorial primary on September 1, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the percentage of the total vote that Michael Roger Minogue receives in the Massachusetts Republican primary for Governor held on September 1, 2026. Only two candidates appear on the ballot: Minogue and Brian Shortsleeve. The value is Minogue's votes divided by all votes cast in that Republican gubernatorial primary (including any write-in and blank/all-others totals counted toward the race), expressed as a percentage. For example, if Minogue receives 61.4% of the vote, this resolves as 61.4. Resolution is based on results reported by the Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth's Elections Division (https://electionstats.state.ma.us/), or, before official certification, on Associated Press reporting or other [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
reference_class: Contested two-candidate Massachusetts statewide gubernatorial primaries in the modern era (2014 Baker-Fisher, 2018 Baker-Lively): party-endorsed, heavily-funded frontrunner vs. a ballot-qualified but underfunded challenger; winner's share of all ballots cast including blanks
dispersion_basis: SD of final-share error in this exact reference class: 2014 poll-implied 83.6% two-way vs 74.2% actual (9.4pp), 2018 MassINC 80.5% vs 63.9% (16.6pp); plus n=209 subsample MoE 5.8-8.7pp and 18% undecided at 20 days out. SD ~6.8 x 2.56 = 17.4
reasoning: Reference class of two-candidate MA GOP gubernatorial primaries (Baker-Fisher 2014: 73.1%; Baker-Lively 2018: 62.6% of all ballots) gives a base rate near 68 for the endorsed, funded frontrunner. The Aug 5-12 UMass poll (53-26, 18% undecided) implies 67% two-way on proportional allocation and 64% on an even undecided split; June UNH matched at 67%, and the May Suffolk number was higher. Minogue also holds a 70.4-15.5 convention endorsement, a ~13:1 money edge, and leads every demographic crosstab. Cutting against: MA GOP primary polls have systematically understated the challenger (16.6pp two-way shrink in 2018, 9.4pp in 2014), Shortsleeve is running final-week TV attacks on an ad-defined self-funder who refuses to debate, and blanks/all-others (~2% of ballots in 2018) sit in the denominator. I discount the 2018 shrink by about half because its driver -- an intensely mobilized anti-establishment right -- is inverted here: Shortsleeve is the pro-choice Baker-world candidate who took only 15.5% of activist delegates, while Minogue leads conservatives 55-23. The hot Markey-Moulton Democratic primary should also pull unenrolled moderates onto the other ballot, leaving a more registered-Republican, endorsement-following electorate. Center 64.5 with wide, mildly left-skewed bars. Left escape (2%) prices a genuine upset losing by 10+, which the winner markets deem unlikely; right escape (1%) would need Shortsleeve under ~13%, below any modern MA two-candidate loser.
what_would_change_my_mind: A final-week independent poll (Suffolk/Globe, UMass, or Emerson) showing the two-way gap narrowing below 20 points, or Shortsleeve above 32%
Evidence that Shortsleeve's 'election fraud' attack is landing in earned media or that a major MassGOP/conservative-media bloc has swung to him
A Trump or high-profile MAGA endorsement for either candidate before Sept. 1
Early-vote or party-registration data showing unusually high unenrolled participation in the GOP primary (which historically has fed the anti-frontrunner column)
Confirmation that blanks/all-others in the GOP gubernatorial primary run materially above the 2.0% seen in 2018, which mechanically lowers Minogue's share of total ballots

question: What will the most recent WHO Disease Outbreak News report as the cumulative confirmed Ebola deaths in the DRC, as of September 4, 2026?

The figure used is the cumulative number of confirmed deaths in the DRC (not the multi-country outbreak total, and not probable/suspected deaths). For example, if the latest DON states "4,665 confirmed cases and 2,184 deaths" in the DRC, this resolves as 2184.
reference_class: WHO Disease Outbreak News items issued for the 2026 DRC Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak (n=10, 29 May - 14 Aug 2026): their inter-publication gaps, their publication-to-data lag, and the per-DON increment in the DRC cumulative confirmed-death figure
dispersion_basis: Bimodal mixture, not a single SD: a ~10% atom at exactly 2184 (no new DON; DON615 stands) plus a continuous branch. Continuous branch itself = 4-9 days of deaths at 41 +/- 7 per day from the 22 Aug national figure of ~2643, convolved with +/-1-2 days of publication-date uncertainty (each day ~41 deaths) and ~+/-30 for WHO-vs-national harmonisation discrepancy, giving branch SDs of ~70 (data 24-27 Aug) and ~105 (data 28 Aug-1 Sep). The atom is what makes the 10-90 width 826 rather than ~300.

Since mid-June the inter-DON gap has been 14, 14, 15, 13 days with a rock-steady 2-day data lag, and the DRC confirmed-death increment per DON was +220, +376, +759, +597 — a naive class anchor of 2184 + ~580 = ~2764. Adjusting on actual surveillance: deaths ran 2184 (12 Aug) to ~2643 (22 Aug), i.e. ~46/day decelerating to ~43/day as case incidence plateaus near 85/day at CFR ~47%; projecting 41/day to a data-as-of date of ~26 Aug gives ~2807. DON616-619 all 404, so no DON of any kind since 14 Aug — exactly what the fortnightly pattern predicts, with the next due 27-29 Aug, comfortably before the 3 Sep 23:59 UTC instant. Main downside risk is not a slower epidemic but a missed publication: no gap in this outbreak has exceeded 15 days (0/7), yet WHO already issues weekly AFRO external situation reports that could absorb DON duty, so I hold ~10% on the 2184 floor rather than the ~2% a pure gap-distribution fit would give. Upside comes from slippage, not severity — a DON published 31 Aug-3 Sep would carry data as of 29 Aug-1 Sep and read 2950-3080. Escape masses are thin but named: below 2100 needs a downward confirmed-to-probable reclassification during the harmonisation WHO explicitly flags (2%); above 3800 needs a retrospective backlog dump or ~110 deaths/day sustained (1.5%). No prediction market prices this contract, so no crowd blend. Note the question background's '5 August DON, 4053/1850' does not match any DON I could retrieve — DON614 (1 Aug) reported 3605/1587 as of 30 July, and DON615's own '+1060 cases, +597 deaths since 1 August' reconciles to DON614, so I anchored on the DONs themselves.
what_would_change_my_mind: A new Ebola DON appearing before 3 Sep — its stated data-as-of date and DRC confirmed-death figure would collapse nearly all uncertainty
The gap passing 29 Aug with still no DON616+, which would break the 13-15 day pattern and push meaningful mass onto both the 2184 atom and the later/higher data-as-of branch
A WHO statement that DON reporting for this outbreak is being replaced by the weekly AFRO external situation reports
Daily death counts moving materially off ~40-46/day (a jump above 60/day or a drop below 25/day) in the 24 Aug - 1 Sep national updates

question: How many named storms will the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season have had by September 5, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question asks for the cumulative number of named tropical storms in the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season that had formed on or before September 5, 2026 (i.e. that were assigned a name from the Atlantic naming list at any point through that date). It resolves based on the National Hurricane Center's 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season summary table at https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/index.php?season=2026&basin=atl — specifically, the count of distinct named systems (those listed with a name such as Arthur, Bertha, etc.) whose first attainment of tropical-storm or subtropical-storm status (the start of the "Dates active" range) fell on or before September 5, 2026 (UTC). A system is counted if it was named on or before September 5, 2026, regardless of its later intensity (a system that strengthened into a hurricane still counts as one named storm). For example, if six named systems had formed through September 5, the question resolves as 6.
reference_class: Atlantic hurricane seasons in a suppressed/El-Nino-shear regime with 3 or fewer named storms formed by ~Aug 21 (1983, 1987, 1988, 1992, 1993, 1997, 2002, 2009, 2013, 2014, 2015), measured by their cumulative named-storm count on Sep 5
dispersion_basis: SD of Aug21->Sep5 named-storm increments across 11 suppressed/El-Nino analog seasons (0,0,1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,3; SD ~1.1) x 2.56 = 2.8, widened to 3.4 for regime-break risk in both directions
reasoning: Count is 3 (Arthur, Bertha, Cristobal) with ~12 days to run. NHC's 24 Aug 06Z outlook flags only two areas: AL95 near Bermuda (50%/50%, i.e. now-or-never) and an east-Atlantic wave (10% two-day, 50% seven-day); netting out the depression-to-named haircut gives ~0.75 expected names from those two, plus ~0.5 from not-yet-flagged genesis in the Sep 1-5 peak. That +1.25 bottom-up sits just under the +1.6 reference-class increment; I take +1.4, median 4. Record Caribbean shear and a strong El Nino (slowest ACE start since 1988; ACE ~3.1) argue low, but named-storm COUNT is far more forgiving than ACE - weak short-lived subtropical systems still get names - and CPC sees shear relaxing 26 Aug-8 Sep. Closest analog 2014 shared the same three names and reached exactly 4 by Sep 5. Right tail is real (2002 and 2015 added 3 in this window) but P(>=10) is negligible, so no upper escape declared.
what_would_change_my_mind: AL95 being upgraded to Tropical Storm Dolly in the next 48 hours (removes the single largest source of downside), or conversely NHC dropping it to 0-20%
NHC 7-day genesis odds for the east-Atlantic wave rising above 70% or falling below 20% in the next few outlooks
CPC's next GTHO raising eastern-MDR genesis above 40% or showing the MJO stalling constructively over the Atlantic rather than retreating to the Indian Ocean
Any sign of a Gulf/western-Caribbean homegrown genesis signal in the Sep 1-5 range, which would add mass above 5
Evidence that Caribbean/MDR shear has broken below climatology rather than merely relaxing

A launch counts once the vehicle lifts off from the pad, regardless of mission outcome. Resolution is based on the running year-to-date tally stated on the Wikipedia article "List of Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launches" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Falcon_9_and_Falcon_Heavy_launches), which maintains a sentence of the form "As of [date], SpaceX has conducted N Falcon family vehicle launches ... in 2026." The value is the count of launches dated on or before September 3, 2026 in that article's 2026 flight table. For example, if 106 Falcon-family launches have occurred in 2026 by that date, this resolves as 106.
reference_class: Falcon-family launch counts over ~11-day windows during SpaceX's 2025-2026 high-cadence era (mean ~4.7 launches per 11 days, SD ~1.8), applied to the confirmed base of 100 launches through Aug 23, 2026
dispersion_basis: Poisson(lambda=4.9) count over the 10.5-day window has a 10-90 width of ~6.0; shaded to 5.0 for the manifest-driven under-dispersion of a scheduled launch program, then carried at 5.5 in the declared percentiles
reasoning: Base is effectively known: SpaceX confirmed its 100th Falcon-family launch of 2026 (99 F9 + 1 FH) on Aug 22-23 UTC, and nothing appears to have flown Aug 23-24 (next scheduled is Aug 25). So this is purely a count of launches over the 10.5 days from now to Sep 3 23:59 UTC. Reference class of 2026 Falcon cadence gives 0.426/day (100 in 235 days); trailing-August is hotter at ~0.50/day (90th F9 on Aug 4 to 99th on Aug 22); per-pad decomposition gives ~4.5. Center on ~4.9 additional launches, i.e. 105. Downside: early September is the Atlantic hurricane-season peak, the Aug 30 Falcon Heavy/Roman campaign occupies 39A and takes range priority, and the year's pace (155/yr) is already slightly below 2025's 165 as resources shift to Starship. Upside: SpaceX routinely bursts multiple launches per day across three pads and has four named Starlink groups queued. Published schedules show only ~4 in-window missions but reliably undercount unannounced Starlink slots, so I do not treat that as evidence of a slowdown. Polymarket/Kalshi price only full-year, all-vehicle SpaceX counts (140-159 @59%; ~156 implied) - contract mismatch on vehicle set, deadline, and source, so used as weak corroboration of pace only, not as an anchor.

question: Will a 7th DRC province be reported as affected by the 2026 Ebola outbreak, as of September 3, 2026?

It resolves NO if the most recent such report as of September 3, 2026 states that six or fewer DRC provinces have been affected. WHO DONs can be found at https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news . As of August 21, 2026, the most recent WHO DON (14 August 2026) listed six affected provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, and Bas-Uélé.
reference_class: New-province additions in the 2026 DRC Bundibugyo outbreak after the initial May multi-province seeding (Haut-Uele 29 Jun, Tshopo 30 Jun, Bas-Uele 13 Aug), combined with the observed WHO DON publication cadence for this same outbreak
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent runs [0.16, 0.14, 0.19] -> 0.162; the narrative below is the research run's own view (0.16)]
Two conjunctive conditions: a 7th province must be confirmed AND a WHO DON stating it must publish by 3 Sep 2026; absent a new DON the question defaults NO off the 14 Aug DON (six provinces). Reference class of province additions in this outbreak post-initial-seeding gives ~1 per 32 days (gaps of 39 and 44 days between the last three additions), implying ~22% over the ~8-day effective detection window before a DON data cutoff. WHO DON cadence on this outbreak (23/25/29/13-day gaps; last on 14 Aug) makes a new DON in the 20-day window roughly a coin flip, though DONs appear event-triggered by new-province detection (Bas-Uele: detected 12-13 Aug, in the 14 Aug DON within ~2 days), so the two conditions are positively correlated. Against: last three weeks of incidence is confined to Ituri/N.Kivu/Haut-Uele, the three peripheral provinces are single-introduction and contained, no alerts reported in unaffected provinces, and response capacity is scaling. For: fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record (~5,515 confirmed, ~51/day), six provinces now border many unaffected ones, high mobility and insecurity.

WHO reclassifying Kinshasa (which has had a laboratory-confirmed case since 16 May per Wikipedia) into its cumulative affected-province list
Evidence that WHO has shifted this outbreak from DONs to AFRO weekly sitreps only, making no DON in the window near-certain
Reports of a probable/suspect case under investigation in a new province in the 25 Aug – 1 Sep daily sitreps

missing_evidence: ['No stated WHO policy on DON publication triggers/schedule for this outbreak, so the publication gate is inferred from observed cadence', 'WHO AFRO Weekly External Situation Report 15 (data ~23 Aug) not yet retrieved; it would be the earliest signal of a 7th-province detection']

No stated WHO policy on DON publication triggers or cadence for this outbreak, so the publication leg is inferred from only five observed gaps (23, 25, 29, 13 days); also no visibility into suspect-case surveillance in provinces adjacent to Bas-Uele and South Kivu.

question: What will the daily global-mean surface air temperature be on September 3, 2026 (ERA5)?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the daily global-mean 2-metre surface air temperature ("World" area, 90°S–90°N) for 3 September 2026, in degrees Celsius, from the ERA5 reanalysis as reported by the Copernicus Climate Change Service "Climate Pulse" tool (https://pulse.climate.copernicus.eu/), reading the "Global surface air temperature" daily value for that date. For example, a value of 16.98 °C resolves as 16.98. If Climate Pulse does not display a value for 3 September 2026 at the resolution snapshot, the equivalent ERA5 "World" daily value for 3 September 2026 from Climate Reanalyzer's Daily Surface Air Temperature time series (https://climatereanalyzer.org/clim/t2_daily/) is used instead.
reference_class: ERA5 daily global-mean 2 m surface air temperature on 3 September, 2015-2025 (reconstructed as clim 15.77 + that September's published monthly anomaly)
dispersion_basis: SD of the 15-day change in the daily global-mean anomaly over Aug19->Sep3 in 2023/2024/2025 (+0.22, +0.01, +0.17) ~ 0.12, combined in quadrature with ~0.08 uncertainty in the current anomaly level (July bulletin implies +0.67-0.75; the quoted 19-Aug reading implies +0.90) and ~0.04 climatology-interpolation error -> SD ~0.145, x2.56 = 0.37, widened to 0.40 for the mixture over two level frameworks
reasoning: Climatological 3 Sep in ERA5 is ~15.77 C, derived from Copernicus bulletins (Aug clim 16.11, Sep clim 15.45, cross-checked on 2023/2024/2025). The forecast is therefore 15.77 + the anomaly. The value is computed as the August 2026 seasonally adjusted Government employment level minus the July 2026 seasonally adjusted Government employment level, both from the "Government" total line of Table B-1, expressed in thousands. reasoning: Reference class (August SA government change, 2015-2025 ex-2020) centers near +16 with SD ~24 - August is normally a modest positive month. question: What will Casas Bahia (BHIA3) shares close at on the last B3 trading day on or before September 4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the official closing price of Grupo Casas Bahia S.A. ordinary shares (ticker BHIA3) on the B3 exchange for the last regular trading session that occurs on or before September 4, 2026, in Brazilian reais (R$). For example, a close of R$0.43 resolves as 0.43. The resolution value is taken from the "Close" value for that date on the Status Invest history page (https://statusinvest.com.br/acoes/bhia3) or, if unavailable, the Yahoo Finance historical page (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BHIA3.SA/history/) or other credible sources.
reference_class: B3-listed equities trading as penny stocks in the second-to-fourth week after a recuperacao judicial filing, after the initial filing-day crash (e.g. AMER3 Jan-Feb 2023, OIBR3 Jun-Jul 2016, LIGT3 2024)
dispersion_basis: Daily log-return SD of BHIA3 over the last 30 sessions is 5.7% excluding the Aug-17 filing gap (11.4% including it); bumped to 7%/day for live-RJ headline risk, x sqrt(8.5 remaining sessions) = 0.204 log-SD, x 2.563 = 0.523 log width, applied around a 0.39 median = 0.21 in R$.
reasoning: Anchor: BHIA3 last closed 0.41 (Aug 24) and trades 0.40-0.41 today, having chopped in a 0.41-0.44 band for six sessions since the Aug-17 RJ filing gap; 8 B3 sessions remain to Fri Sept 4 (no holiday intervenes). Reference class of penny-priced equities 2-4 weeks after an RJ/Chapter-11 filing gives a median ~10-session forward return near -5% with very fat two-sided tails, so I take 0.41 -> ~0.39 rather than a flat martingale: negative equity, R$17.3bn of senior claims and expected dilution make this a deep-OTM lottery ticket, the drift since the filing is about -1.4%/session, and Ibovespa rebalancing flow (3rd previa Aug 31, new portfolio effective the week of Sept 7) concentrates forced selling of a sub-R$1 name right at the Sept 4 close. Against that: the price has genuinely stabilised for six sessions, the 1-centavo tick makes each down-step a full 2.4% so grinding lower is slow, and any DIP-financing or plan headline pops these names 20-30% in a session -- hence the right-skewed 0.52 p90. Both bounds are essentially unreachable: >R$1.00 needs +144%, and the only clean mechanism (a grupamento, which BHIA3 ran 25:1 in Dec 2023) has no 2026 convocation and historically took ~2 months from proposal to grouped trading; <R$0.15 needs -63%, requiring conversion to falencia inside 8 sessions after the RJ was already accepted. No human prediction market prices this, so the number is unanchored by any crowd.
what_would_change_my_mind: A confirmed DIP financing agreement or credible investor injection announced before Sept 4 (a fato relevante, not press speculation the CVM forces the company to deny) — would shift the median toward 0.45-0.55
Announcement of a grupamento/reverse split with an effective date on or before Sept 4 — would move nearly all mass above the upper bound
Court conversion of the RJ to falencia, denial of the recovery plan's processing, or a CVM/B3 trading suspension — would push the median under 0.25 and fatten p_below_lower sharply
B3's 3rd Ibovespa previa (Aug 31) or the final portfolio confirming BHIA3's removal, plus visible tracker volume — would tilt the Sept 4 close 1-3 cents lower
Two or more consecutive sessions closing above 0.46 or below 0.36, which would break the six-session 0.40-0.44 regime and re-centre the median
